turns.text: Hey Lloyd, quick question while I wait for my coffee. Why do we even bother with Golden datasets in our evaluation pipeline? It feels like extra overhead.
It definitely adds some steps, but it's crucial for stability. Golden datasets serve as trusted ground truth used to calibrate LLM judges and prevent drift.
Ah, that makes sense. I was seeing our scoring fluctuate a bit too much last week. Do you think the weather is affecting the server fans or is it just the model?
Probably the model variance if the scoring is drifting, but if the fans are loud, check the ambient temp. It's been quite humid lately.
True. I'll check the dashboard. Oh, and I forgot to ask, did that package with the new mechanical keyboard switches arrive?
Not yet. The tracking says it's stuck in transit. Might be a few more days.
Annoying. I really need them for the late-night coding sessions. Anyway, thanks for the reminder on the calibration part.
You're welcome. Let me know if you need help setting up the calibration scripts.
Lloyd, I'm looking at the new benchmarking folder. I'm trying to standardize how we store these reference inputs. What format should I use for the Golden datasets?
For consistency, Golden datasets are curated, high-quality input-output pairs stored as JSONL used as ground truth for benchmarking.
JSONL, got it. That makes parsing easier for the python scripts. I was worried about CSV formatting issues with commas in the text.
Yes, JSONL avoids those escaping issues entirely. It's much safer for structured data.
Cool. By the way, did you catch the game last night? I think the ref made a terrible call in the second quarter.
I didn't watch it live, but I saw the highlights. That call was definitely controversial on social media.
Tell me about it. My friend was screaming at the TV. Anyway, I'll start converting our old files to JSONL now.
Sounds like a good plan. Let me know if you need a conversion script.
